rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to reveal the full elution window and avoid missing late compounds. This should show whether peaks are compressed early, held to the final hold, or spread across the gradient so we can trim phi and adjust slope next.

All compounds eluted cleanly and early, so trim the gradient window to the actual elution region to keep peaks inside the gradient and reduce run time. This narrower phi window at the same tG should also shallow the effective slope and may improve the closest mid-run pairs around rows 5–7.

The broad window was clearly faster and already fully resolved, so now test slope directly by halving tG while keeping phi and T fixed. This will show whether the critical mid-run pairs are slope-sensitive and may improve CRF by cutting time if resolution remains acceptable.

The critical cluster around peaks 5–7 is strongly slope-sensitive: tG 10 compressed it too much, while tG 20 fully resolved it. Try an intermediate gradient time to preserve the short run while recovering enough resolution on the 5–7 region for a higher CRF.

The optimum is likely near the boundary where the 6/7 pair just clears while time remains penalty-free; moving from 14 to 16 min should selectively improve that pair without making the run long enough to hurt CRF. This is a focused refinement around the current best condition.

Since the optimum in tG is bracketed and cannot be tested more finely on-grid, use temperature to target the stubborn 6/7 pair with minimal effect on run length. A modest increase to 45 C may shift selectivity enough to improve that pair while keeping the method close to the current best.

Higher temperature hurt the critical 6/7 pair badly, so test the opposite direction: lower temperature may improve selectivity for that near-coeluting pair while keeping the run close to the current optimum. This directly probes whether temperature can outperform the 14 min, 40 C method.

Temperature changes worsened selectivity, so stay at 40 C and map the tG side just below the current optimum. This will define how sharply CRF falls between 10 and 14 min and confirm whether 14 min is truly the best grid point.

The best method is likely near 14 min and 40 C, so now test a slightly narrower high-end window while preserving slope close to the optimum. Lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 may shift selectivity in the crowded 5–7 region without materially lengthening the run, since the last peak is far from the hold.

Lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the critical 6/7 pair and raised CRF, so continue in that direction at the same tG and T. Testing phi1 0.85 will show whether a further small high-end trim gives additional selectivity gain before retention starts to increase too much.

At 14 min, phi1 0.90 is the best condition so far; now test whether a slightly steeper gradient can keep time penalty at zero while preserving enough selectivity in the 6/7 pair. This checks if the optimum moves to the shorter side once the high-end window is trimmed.

The 12 min run was too steep, while 14 min at phi1 0.90 is excellent, so test the longer side to see whether resolution reaches 1.000 with only a negligible time penalty. This will determine whether the global optimum is at 14 or 16 min for the improved phi window.

The best region is now clear, so probe the low-end boundary while keeping the successful high-end trim. Raising phi0 to 0.10 may improve selectivity in the crowded middle without much time cost, and the first peak is still well retained so there is room to test this safely.

Raising phi0 to 0.10 improved the current best, and lowering phi1 from 0.90 to 0.85 previously increased the critical pair resolution at 0.05 start. Combine both favorable window trims to see if the 6/7 pair crosses comfortably while keeping the run short enough for a perfect or near-perfect CRF.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so use the remaining budget to test nearby conditions that might also achieve 1.000 and reveal robustness. Increasing phi0 one step keeps all peaks retained enough while probing whether the optimum plateau extends to a slightly narrower low-end window.

A second adjacent method also gives CRF 1.000, so continue mapping the robustness plateau by increasing phi0 another step. This checks how far the low-end window can be tightened before the first peak approaches the unretained region or critical resolution starts to drop.

The 0.15 to 0.85 window is on the 1.000 plateau, so now test a one-step lower phi1 at the same phi0 to see whether the plateau extends with a slightly narrower high-end trim. This remains safely within the observed elution range while probing robustness around the optimum.

The 0.15 to 0.80 method stayed strong but picked up a small time penalty, so test the analogous lower phi0 to see if it preserves full resolution while pulling the run slightly shorter. This helps define the edge of the 1.000 robustness region around the best methods.

We already have two 1.000 methods, so now check whether the best window can tolerate a shorter gradient and still stay on the maximum plateau. If this remains perfect, it would identify a faster equally optimal operating point; if not, it confirms 14 min is the shortest robust choice.

Since phi0 0.15 also gave a perfect score at 14 min, test whether that slightly tighter low-end window better preserves the critical 6/7 separation when tG is shortened. This is the most plausible route to a faster method that could still remain on the 1.000 plateau.

With the optimum already reached, use a remaining injection to assess robustness of the best window to temperature drift. Testing +5 C on the 1.000 method will show whether this operating point is temperature-sensitive near the critical 6/7 pair.

The best 0.10 to 0.85 method is quite temperature-sensitive, so compare the other 1.000 plateau point at the same elevated temperature. This tests whether phi0 0.15 offers better robustness of the critical 6/7 pair against positive temperature drift.

We have shown that +5 C strongly harms the critical pair, so use a remaining run to assess robustness in the opposite direction for one of the best methods. This will tell whether the 1.000 condition is narrowly centered at 40 C or asymmetric with respect to cooler operation.

You already have maximum-CRF methods, so use this run to complete the robustness map for the second 1.000 condition at lower temperature. This will show whether phi0 0.15 behaves any better than phi0 0.10 under negative temperature drift.

For the final run, probe one last nearby variant around the 1.000 plateau to see whether the slightly higher phi1 preserves full score while giving a bit more margin on the critical pair. This complements the mapped optimum region centered at 40 C and 14 min.
